question: In what year did the painter Idris Penhallow-Vane hold his first solo exhibition?
document: Idris Penhallow-Vane was born in 1931 in the river town of Aldmere, the youngest of four children of a sign painter and a schoolteacher. He spent his boyhood lettering shopfronts beside his father, an apprenticeship he later credited with his obsessive attention to edges and spacing. After two unhappy years studying law, he abandoned his degree and enrolled at the Corran School of Fine Art, where he fell under the influence of the colourist Mabli Torrance. Penhallow-Vane held his first solo exhibition in the year he turned twenty-four, showing eleven small canvases of flooded fields in a borrowed room above a bakery. Only two sold, but one of them was bought by the critic Lionel Graft, whose enthusiastic review brought the young painter his first commissions. Over the following decades he developed the layered, almost translucent style of his mature landscapes, and by the time of his death he had completed more than six hundred paintings. A retrospective of his work toured three cities in the year after he died, and his studio in Aldmere is now maintained as a small museum.

document: Aurelie Fenwick-Strand was among the most influential philologists of her generation, known for her painstaking reconstructions of the lost dialects of the Ostmarch valleys. That work established her international reputation and led to visiting appointments in several countries. In later life she became an outspoken advocate for the preservation of regional archives, many of which were at risk of being dispersed or destroyed.
